title: Casper and the Letter
premise: In 1890s river-port Brannock's Landing, Wendell Montrose, a pearl diver's daughter indentured to the Halloway Trading Company, keeps her head down mending nets and ledgers. When an infant is abandoned at the workshop door with a note ordering the finder to forget her face, Wendell cannot — and neither can the child's hidden kin, who will do anything to bury the evidence of a powerful family's crime. As spring ice threatens to break on the river and the company moves to demolish the workshop that shelters them, Wendell uncovers a letter proving the child is heir to everything Halloway stole. She must choose between her indenture and justice outside the law: she smuggles the letter and the baby upriver before the ice breaks, wins the child a home with the diver community that becomes her found family, and burns her own contract in the process.
about_author: Hazel Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing shipping ledgers from forgotten river towns. She writes historical fiction about the people those ledgers were never meant to remember.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Hands
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. We meet her at sixteen, indentured to Halloway Trading Company, mending nets by lamplight while the workshop sleeps. She recalls her father's drowning and the debt that bound her. Emotional beat: quiet endurance, the discipline of being unnoticed.

chapters.title: Left at the Door
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A freezing night; a knock no one answers. She finds an infant wrapped in oilcloth with a note: 'Forget this face.' No footprints but one set, already filling with snow. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant tenderness as she takes the child inside.

chapters.title: The Company's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Foreman Aldous Pike discovers the baby and demands it be gone by morning — children are liabilities on the ledger. Wendell hides her in the net loft. Emotional beat: first open defiance, fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Maren of the Divers
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She seeks out Maren Oduya, an old pearl diver and her late father's friend, who agrees to help but warns that whoever left the child will come back for silence, not gratitude. Emotional beat: the first thread of found family.

chapters.title: A Face Worth Forgetting
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: brief chapter from the watcher — a hired man named Corliss — reporting to an unseen employer that the child was seen alive. Emotional beat: menace entering the story; the reader knows what Wendell only suspects.

chapters.title: The Workshop That Remembers
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Searching the loft for cloth for the baby, she finds a hidden cache: letters, a woman's ring, and one sealed envelope addressed in a hand she recognizes from company ledgers. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into danger.

chapters.title: Ice Groaning on the River
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The river ice begins to shift early this year; the town talks of flood. Pike announces Halloway will sell the workshop lot to be razed before thaw. Emotional beat: the clock starts ticking — two deadlines, water and demolition.

chapters.title: The Name in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Cross-referencing dates in the stolen letters against company records, she realizes the child belongs to a woman who died asking Halloway for what was hers. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger, and the birth of purpose.

chapters.title: Corliss Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A polite stranger offers Wendell money for 'anything the mother may have left.' She lies well for the first time in her life. Emotional beat: terror mastered; she understands they will kill for the paper.

chapters.title: What Maren Dived For
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Flashback to the pearl beds and Wendell's father, who once hid a client's secrets at the bottom of the river. Maren reveals he helped the child's mother once too. Emotional beat: Wendell inherits not just a duty but a legacy.

chapters.title: The Letter, Opened
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She breaks the seal: a confession naming Halloway's theft of the mother's inheritance, witnessed and dated. It names the child as rightful heir. Emotional beat: awe and horror — she holds a weapon made of ink.

chapters.title: Pike's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Pike catches her with company papers and offers a terrible trade: the letter for her freedom papers. Wendell stalls, heartsick, tempted. Emotional beat: the cost of justice made personal.

chapters.title: Fire Watch
chapters.summary: Corliss's POV. Ordered to burn the workshop and let the thaw hide the ashes, Corliss hesitates — the child cried when he carried her once. Emotional beat: the hunter cracking; the reader sees his conscience wake.

chapters.title: The Night of Smoke
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Fire in the drying shed. Wendell saves the baby and the letter through the smoke; Maren pulls her out half-conscious. The workshop survives, barely. Emotional beat: loss and fury; no more hiding.

chapters.title: Witnesses in the Net Loft
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The divers' community shelters them openly now. An old clerk, Tobias Finch, recognizes the witness signature on the letter — a man still living upriver. Emotional beat: hope with a route attached; allies gather.

chapters.title: The Demolition Notice
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Halloway posts final notice: the workshop falls in six days, right at expected ice-break. Pike, ashamed of the fire, quietly tells Wendell which night the wreckers come. Emotional beat: betrayal inside the enemy; the deadline narrows.

chapters.title: Corliss Turns His Coat
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Corliss delivers proof of his employer's orders to Wendell instead, choosing the child over the coin. He gives them the name: Edwina Halloway herself. Emotional beat: redemption offered and accepted warily.

chapters.title: Upstream Before the Break
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. With Maren, Corliss, and the baby hidden in a pearling skiff, they slip upriver at night as the ice groans apart behind them. Pursuers launch. Emotional beat: breathless flight, the river both road and threat.

chapters.title: The Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The thaw surges mid-river; their pursuers' boat is swamped while the skiff rides the flood to Finch's witness. The letter is signed into record as the water tears the town's old order apart. Emotional beat: climax — nature itself rules in their favor.

chapters.title: What the Law Wouldn't Do
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The witness testifies; Halloway's fraud surfaces publicly. But the courts move slowly, so the divers act faster: they claim the workshop lot by salvage and old river-right, holding it until the law catches up. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, communal and fierce.

chapters.title: Burning the Contract
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Freed by the scandal, Wendell is offered her indenture back with honors. Instead she feeds the contract to the stove that kept the baby warm. Emotional beat: liberation chosen, not granted; grief for her father finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: The Face We Kept
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, epilogue tone. Spring on the rebuilt dock: the child — named Pearl — toddles between Maren, Corliss, and Wendell, who signs her new ledger as keeper of the workshop. Emotional beat: memory honored, family made, the face no one forgot now known by everyone.
